propositions: Blocking links between siblings (two direct children of the same parent) currently fail to record because type-tier comparability promotes them upward; must record directly with no escalation.

Type-tier comparability (epic tier 2, story tier 1, task/bug tier 0) allows ancestor-blocking edges (e.g. epic depends_on its own child) to be written because the resolved pair is never re-checked for redundancy.

Structural comparability using nearest common ancestor must replace type-tier; two endpoints escalate to the first pair of direct children of their shared ancestor, or stay unchanged if already siblings or in an ancestor-descendant relationship.

Redundancy guard for blocking links must evaluate the RESOLVED pair for ancestor-descendant relationship, not the original pair, to catch escalated edges that become invalid (e.g. promoted epic-to-child becomes redundant).
Non-blocking relations (relates_to, supersedes, discovered_from) must retain original redundancy logic and gain no new rejections; they are not escalated.
The _get_ancestors ancestor chain walk must remove its max_hops=2 cap to support deep hierarchies and must cycle-guard with a visited set to terminate on malformed parent cycles.
